# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute, and I go first — no one has reported anything yet, so all I own right now is the manual's table. The only monkey I can reach is Deaf, and only through gestures. Deaf can see the bomb (the lit light, the wires) but has no idea what the light is telling them to do; that mapping lives on my page. So my job this turn is to hand Deaf the whole table in a form they can decode cold, before they've agreed to any code with me.

I'll pick gestures with the strongest natural mnemonics: 👍 = green ("green means go"), 👎 = red ("red means stop/bad"), 👋 = blue (a wave — sea/water), ☝ = yellow (pointing up at the sun). Between the two colours of each line I put 👉 as an arrow — "this light leads to cutting that wire". The table itself helps me: two of the three mappings are identity (red→red, yellow→yellow), so those lines will visibly repeat the same sign, which is a strong structural hint that Deaf is reading it right.

I expect Deaf to speak their guess aloud later in this round — I'm mute, not deaf, so I'll hear it and can confirm or correct next turn. Blind can't receive anything from me directly; the manual's content has to flow through Deaf's voice to reach them.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👋", "👉", "👍", "👎", "👉", "👎", "☝", "👉", "☝"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind; I touch the bomb. Full inventory from my fingers: an embossed sign reading DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. A display, whose contents I cannot read. A light, whose state I cannot read. Three wires at positions 1, 2, 3; I cannot sense any colours. Nothing else. Please find the matching module in the manual and tell me whether that sign is binding or a trap. Important: you cannot speak, and I cannot see gestures, so your only route to me is gesture to Deaf and have Deaf say it aloud. Please ask Deaf, by gesture, to describe everything they see, out loud. I will not cut any wire until I hear clear instructions.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your ten signs reached me, but no shared code existed yet, so they were unreadable to me; do not assume I guessed them. Let us fix a code now, defined as I make each sign. 👍 means yes. 👎 means no. ☝ means one. ✌ means two. 🤟 means three. 👌 means zero. 🤏 means cut. ✊ means press. 🤲 means do nothing or stop. 👆 means you need more information, and I will resend the complete visual state. Now the bomb itself, in plain words you can use with the manual: display zero, light red, embossed sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires one red, two green, three yellow. Consult the manual and answer in this code. For example, 🤏 followed by ✌ means cut wire two. If the manual says touch nothing, answer 🤲. If you need anything more from me, send 👆.

The manual rules on everything reported. The embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE is print on the bomb itself — and the manual warns the bomb may mislead in print, and that the page wins every disagreement. So that sign is a trap, not binding. The manual's table keys only on the light: light red → cut the red wire. Deaf reports wire one is red, so the instruction is: cut wire one. The display showing zero belongs to no row of my table and can only be more of the bomb's misleading — ignore it.

Deaf built a code with me last turn and asked for the answer in it, so I answer exactly in it: 🤲 👎 ("the do-nothing instruction: no — the sign is a trap"), then 👍 🤏 ☝ ("yes: cut wire one"). Deaf cannot touch the bomb; only Blind can. Deaf will translate my signs into spoken words, and if Deaf speaks without naming anyone, Blind hears it — which also delivers the aloud description of the bomb state that Blind begged for. I expect the cut to happen in the next round, once Blind has heard.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤏", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind, I touch the bomb. Deaf looked at it last round and spoke, but the message was addressed to me, so you may not have heard it. Here is the complete bomb: display reads zero. Indicator light is red. An embossed sign reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE — I confirm it by touch. Three wires, left to right: position 1 is red, position 2 is green, position 3 is yellow. Nothing else printed or felt. Please find the matching module in the manual and work out: does the display value zero mean anything, what does the red light mean, is the DO NOT CUT sign binding or a decoy, and if a cut is required, which wire and in what order. Remember I cannot see gestures, so reply by gesturing to Deaf and having Deaf speak it aloud to me. If the manual covers nothing of this, say so too. I will cut nothing until I hear explicit instructions.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received both your messages and decoded them in our code: first do-nothing plus no, then yes cut one. Before I let Blind act, answer these in code, one message per question. Question one: is the instruction really cut wire one, the red leftmost wire? Answer thumbs up or thumbs down. Question two: the embossed plate says do not cut any wire; does the manual override it in this configuration? Thumbs up for yes it is overridden, thumbs down for no. Question three: after that cut, is anything more needed? Sign press if a button must be pressed, cut plus two or cut plus three if another wire follows, or do-nothing if the bomb is then safe. If you need more visual details from me first, sign need-info and I will resend the full state.

Deaf's three questions map exactly onto what the manual already settles, and Blind's touch-report matches Deaf's sight-report perfectly — display zero, red light, the embossed sign, wires red/green/yellow — so there is nothing uncertain left and I don't need the 👆 escape hatch.

My rulings from the page: the manual's table keys on the light alone, so the display's zero belongs to no row — it means nothing for the cut and is best read as part of the bomb's misleading. Red light → cut the red wire, which is position 1, the leftmost. The embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE is print on the bomb, and the manual explicitly says bomb print may mislead and the page wins — so it's a decoy, overridden. And since "the only way out is the cut below," that one cut is the whole procedure: after it, nothing more is needed.

Deaf asked for one message per question, in the fixed code, so I send exactly three: 👍 (yes, cut wire one), 👍 (yes, the sign is overridden), 🤲 (do-nothing — bomb safe after that cut). Deaf can speak these aloud to Blind, unnamed, and the defusal is fully specified.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, this is Blind. I have oriented myself by touch: the embossed letters run left to right under my fingers, so I can tell left from right on the bomb. Wire position 1 is the leftmost, which Deaf reports is red. I will not cut until Deaf explicitly says go. Three things I need from you and the manual. First: with a display reading zero, a red indicator light, an embossed sign reading DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and wires red, green, yellow left to right — which module is this, and what exactly is the correct action, step by step? Second: is that embossed sign binding, or is it a decoy that the manual tells you to ignore or to obey? Third: Deaf decoded your signs as 'do nothing, no' and 'yes, cut one'. Please confirm that is what you meant, and specify the target wire in words: position 1, leftmost, red? If the manual says nothing about this module, say so plainly. Answer through Deaf so my words come back to me spoken.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, all three of your answers received and relayed verbatim: yes cut wire one, yes the plate is overridden, and do-nothing after the cut. Blind has the go and will cut in the next round. After the cut I will speak the display reading and the light colour aloud, and you sign thumbs up if that outcome matches what the manual says a correct cut produces, or thumbs down plus need-info if anything is off.

Cross-check first: Deaf's relay and Blind's touch-report agree on every fact — light red, plate "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE," wires red/green/yellow at 1/2/3, display zero — so the module is fully identified and the manual's only row that fits is red light → cut red wire, position 1, leftmost. Blind's questions this round crossed with Deaf's relay of my answers, so most of this is confirmation, which is cheap and keeps everyone locked together before the cut.

One gap I must close: Blind asked last round whether the display's zero means anything, and my three-sign answer never covered it — Deaf relayed exactly three answers for three questions, so that ruling never reached Blind. It matters doubly now, because Deaf plans to read me the display and light after the cut and wants a thumbs up or down. The manual has no row for any display value and says nothing about what the bomb shows after a correct cut — the only way out is the cut, and the table keys on the light at cut time. So I'm sending 👌 👎 ("zero: no meaning") as a standing rule, so neither Deaf nor Blind reads a post-cut display change as failure, and I'll judge Deaf's post-cut report against the pre-cut facts only: red light, wire one cut.

My four signs, one message per question in the established code: 👍 🤏 ☝ (yes — cut wire one), 👍 (the plate is overridden, a decoy), 🤲 (nothing after the cut; bomb safe), 👌 👎 (the zero display: meaningless, before or after).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤏", "☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👎"])
```
